subject: Dedicated perf validation — clarifying streaming concurrency & GPU shortlist
messages:

Subject: Dedicated perf validation — clarifying streaming concurrency & GPU shortlist

Hi Jamie / Alex —

Thanks for the call earlier — good to meet the HealthLynx infra and product teams. Below is my read of the SLOs you shared and the immediate asks we discussed. Please correct me where I’ve misinterpreted anything.

Quick summary of requirements (from your team):
- Client-facing streaming chat: token-by-token WebSocket streaming to mobile clients.
- Latency targets: p95 end-to-end (inference + network shims) <= 250ms for short responses (<=128 tokens); p95 <= 500ms acceptable for longer responses up to ~512 tokens.
- Traffic shape: steady-state ~400 RPS (interactive requests), expected concurrency ~350–450 active connections; peak bursts up to ~1,200 RPS during morning batch windows.
- Typical prompt/response sizes: 90% short prompts (<=64 tokens); 10% long (100–512 tokens).
- Availability expectation: soft SLO 99.9% for pod-level uptime during pilot; eventual Dedicated SLA request TBD.

Initial Redwood read: workload is streaming-forward and latency-sensitive with moderate steady throughput and high concurrency. Effective performance will depend on model choice, quantization, and kernel/path optimizations for streaming KV-cache.

Recommended next steps (action items):
1) HealthLynx: share a small sample prompt corpus (we agreed a 200–300 prompt set) + representative traffic histogram (per-minute RPS distribution for a 24h window). Attachment stub: healthlynx_prompt_samples.txt.
2) Redwood: run a two-phase pilot benchmark (smoke + sustained) using your prompts, comparing 2 GPU shortlists (H100-based and A100-based configs). We’ll produce a bench matrix (redwood_benchmark_matrix.xlsx).
3) Schedule a 30-min pilot planning call next week to finalize network path (VPC peering / private egress), websocket keepalive settings, and data retention constraints.
4) Redwood to send draft pilot SOW and estimated reserved capacity pricing by EOD Friday. Attachment stub: pilot-sow-draft.pdf.

GPU shortlist we proposed on-call (high-level):
- Option A (higher perf / lower node count): 3x NVIDIA H100-80GB (for 13B-class model with dynamic quant and optimized kernels). Expected: better latency headroom for streaming, fewer nodes to manage.
- Option B (balanced perf/cost): 5x NVIDIA A100-80GB (with FP16/4-bit quant profiles). Slightly higher cluster ops overhead but more mature in our fleet.
- Option C (cost-constrained): 6–8x A100 or L40s with aggressive quantization and batching — higher queuing risk under bursty traffic, acceptable if HealthLynx can tolerate higher tail latency during peaks.

High-level perf expectations (estimates — to be validated in pilot):
- H100 pilot (3-node): steady 400 RPS with p95 ~180–230ms on short prompts; burst to ~1,200 RPS with backpressure and graceful queueing depending on batching config.
- A100 pilot (5-node): steady 400 RPS with p95 ~220–300ms on short prompts; burst to ~900–1,100 RPS before latency degradation.

Costs and gating: the pilot will clarify whether we can meet the 250ms p95 target for short responses with A100; if not, H100 is likely required to hit latency SLO without increasing node count.

Please confirm the prompt sample and a preferred slot for the planning call (I’m available Tue/Wed morning PT). Once we have the sample I’ll put together the bench matrix and a proposed pilot schedule.

Thanks,
Rishi
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — this looks right overall. Couple clarifications from our infra side: 
- Websocket layer: we need incremental tokens delivered as soon as they’re produced; we cannot buffer to wait for full response. That rules out any approach that batches across connections for short prompts.
- Network: most clients are mobile on cellular; please assume an extra 40–80ms of network RTT on top of your inferred server-side numbers when sizing.
- For cost modeling: our procurement wants a rough monthly committed cost for both H100 (3-node) and A100 (5-node) pilots so they can compare to cloud VM alternatives.

We’ll attach the requested prompt set and a 24h RPS histogram this afternoon — Alex will upload to the Drive link you sent. 

Two quick questions: 1) Does Redwood’s serving runtime support per-connection KV-cache isolation at scale (we’ll have 350+ connections)? 2) For streaming, do you recommend disabling inter-request batching entirely, or using small intra-request microbatches?

—Jamie
CTO, HealthLynx

Jamie — thanks for the clarifications, and for confirming the drive upload. Quick answers to your two questions and an updated plan: 

1) Per-connection KV-cache: yes — our runtime supports isolated KV caches per session. We’ve validated >1k concurrent active KV sessions in prior pilots. The cost here is memory per session; for 13B-class models we typically budget ~200–600MB of GPU RAM per active session depending on sequence length and kv-cache retention window. We’ll estimate exact numbers once we see your prompt/response length histogram.

2) Batching recommendation for streaming workloads: avoid cross-connection batching for short prompts. For short interactive flows we use dynamic microbatching that only groups tokens within a single connection/request (microbatch size 1–4) to preserve token-level latency. For the background 10% long-response traffic we enable slightly larger batching windows to improve throughput without impacting short-response latency.

Updated pilot plan and sizing heuristics:
- Pilot goals: validate p95 <=250ms short prompt latency (server-side) and confirm sustainable steady-state throughput of 400 RPS with 350–450 concurrent active connections.
- Workload assumptions: avg half of requests return <=64 tokens; avg long responses ~220 tokens.
- Memory sizing: assume 350 active sessions * ~350MB/session ~= 122.5GB GPU RAM consumed by KV caches; that suggests H100-80GB nodes require a multi-node layout with session affinity to avoid thrashing.

Redwood pilot configs we’ll run (smoke + 48h sustained):
A) H100 baseline: 3x H100-80GB with streaming-optimized kernels, KV-cache eviction set to conservative defaults.
B) A100 balanced: 5x A100-80GB with FP16 + 4-bit quant fallbacks for long responses.
C) Cost-minded: 8x A100 with aggressive quant and larger batching windows (to show cost floor).

Deliverables after pilot: bench matrix with p50/p95/p99 latency by prompt size bucket, reserved throughput curves, resource utilization graphs, and an ops checklist for rollout.

Next steps: I’ll ingest your prompt set and histogram once uploaded and kick off the smoke run. Can we lock a 30-min planning slot Thurs 10–10:30am PT? Ben, Soojin — can you join to map the pilot SOW and ops handoff?

Best,
Rishi
